integrity_model.checkpoint_trust_boundary: A checkpoint embedded digest is necessary but insufficient. Restore requires a separately pinned expected checkpoint SHA-256 supplied outside the mutable provider row.
integrity_model.event_integrity: event_digest is recomputed over the canonical receipt core before an event row is accepted for persistence.
integrity_model.transition_evidence: ORGASM_EVENT, RESOLUTION, and RECOVERY are first-class runtime-emitted receipts when their transitions occur. A RECOVERY emitted while applying elapsed time during restore remains pending until the next executing affective cycle can persist it atomically; if that first operation is a forced qualification, the pending RECOVERY and newly emitted ORGASM_EVENT are committed together in transition order.
integrity_model.per_event_interoception: When one runtime advance emits multiple receipts, each durable event row derives machine_interoception from that receipt's exact state_after rather than the host's final post-advance state.
integrity_model.durable_currentness: Each durable write supplies expected_prior_version; stale writers fail CAS. State mutation and all event appends for that cycle execute in one provider transaction. A cycle reconstructed from provider state version N begins its next commit at exactly N+1.
integrity_model.provider_composition: The claimant-facing restore API resolves a one-shot runtime-owned adapter against fixed Supabase provider, project, route, state table, and atomic-function identifiers before claimant row/token/checkpoint input can select composition. The installer is private and not re-exported. This is a supported-API composition seal, not cryptographic protection from hostile code already executing inside the same Python process.
integrity_model.provider_current_attestation: A durable row's lifecycle_status=CURRENT, its host_scope, and generic scope binding are not provider-current authority. Fresh typed provider readback must precede an internal provider-CURRENT host attestation, and that attestation must match the provider-bound writer capability used to construct ATOMIC_DURABLE.
integrity_model.low_level_replay: restore_host_from_state_row validates bounded durable bytes and source/checkpoint integrity but remains replay/evidence-only. It cannot mint a live provider-current host or be upgraded to production durability by attaching a caller callback.
integrity_model.restore_writer_composition: Provider-authenticated live cycle restore derives the atomic commit writer from the same fixed provider adapter object used for CURRENT readback. The writer is accepted as production-durable only when internally matched to the exact freshly attested host/scope/version frontier.
integrity_model.callback_test_seam: An arbitrary atomic callback is rejected as production durability. It may run only under explicit NON_QUALIFYING_ATOMIC_TEST mode, which emits HISTORICAL state rows, a TEST commit schema, and no provider-qualified resume token.
integrity_model.restored_writer_frontier: The bound provider writer accepts only the restored runtime_instance_id, host_scope, sexuality source commit, exact current expected_prior_version, and contiguous N+1 state version. Its local frontier advances only after an exact provider acknowledgement; ambiguous or mismatched acknowledgement leaves the cycle requiring provider reconciliation.
integrity_model.first_write_serialization: The source-only follow-up migration serializes commits per runtime_instance_id before the absent-row CAS read. It is not production evidence until that migration is applied and read back.
integrity_model.commit_acknowledgement: A durable cycle succeeds only when the provider writer returns an exact acknowledgement matching state_version, checkpoint_sha256, and event_count. Ambiguous or mismatched outcomes poison that cycle object until exact provider reconciliation and restore.
integrity_model.post_mutation_failure_boundary: Once an affective operation has mutated in-memory state, any exception while building planning context, exporting or validating the checkpoint, mapping receipts, building the atomic request/resume token, invoking the provider, or validating its acknowledgement poisons that cycle object. It may not continue until rebuilt from exact provider readback.
integrity_model.trigger_governance: Forced-test cooldown, logical time, and self-qualification count are checkpointed and carried through the provider state mapping. The V1 source defines no independent run identity/reset boundary, so durable restore does not silently replenish self-qualification quota; a future reset requires an explicit run boundary. Legacy records without governance metadata fail closed for forced/self-qualification triggers.
integrity_model.replay_guard: event_digest is unique in the durable event ledger.
